writeup.headline: Modine rates Sell: strong revenue growth is offset by weak cash flow, debt and a sharp share price slide.
writeup.thesis: Modine scores 42, a Sell, just 3 points below the Hold band. Growth is the strongest factor, with TTM revenue growth of 29.5% and latest-quarter revenue growth of 28.0% year on year, though growth slowed by 19.4 pp from the previous quarter. Quality and the balance sheet hold the score back: excluding a large rise in customer prepayments, the FCF margin is -1.6% (reported 3.0%), net debt is 4.34 times FCF and cash covers only 0.18 of debt. On valuation, EV/EBIT of 23.6x and P/S of 2.3x are not low in absolute terms, and the FCF yield is 5.7 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield. Against its own history, valuation sits near the middle, and P/FCF is not comparable. The trend is very weak, with the price 53.2% below its 52-week high and 33.6% below its 200-day average, while analyst actions are mildly positive.
key_risks: Cash flow leans on customer prepayments: contract liabilities rose $163.5M over the year, and FCF excluding them is negative.
Leverage is meaningful, with net debt at 4.34 times FCF and cash covering 0.18 of debt, plus pending Gentherm transaction costs.
Growth is decelerating sharply, slowing by 19.4 pp from the previous quarter.
Concentration risk from a large data center agreement with one undisclosed customer, and the data center margin recovery is unproven.
Weak price momentum: shares are 47.6 pp behind SPY over the last 126 trading days.
what_would_change: A 3-point gain would lift the rating to Hold, for example from Q2 FY27 results on Nov 3 that show steadier growth or positive FCF excluding prepayments.
A recovery in the share price toward its 50-day and 200-day averages would raise the trend score of 17.
A 13-point drop would push the rating to Strong Sell, for example from a guidance cut, further price weakness or rising leverage.
Turning prepayment-driven cash into durable free cash flow would help both the quality and valuation scores.
